_comment: v3. First two segments passed all 4 guardrail gates cleanly (clean single-band asphalt mask, detect_road agrees with manual measurement, no competing gray structures). garden.png had a painted-in car removed via tools/strip-car.py before being added here.
_chunking: chunk_height must stay above the full stitched height (~7431px with creek-conclusion.png added) since almost every join past garden-beach.png is a soft overlap:200 blend, not a hard cut - an internal chunk boundary not pinned to a hard cut shows as a faint seam between two separately-rasterized elements even when the pixels either side are identical (the same class of artifact 25aa6c5 fixed once already by merging chunks). Revisit if the route grows past 8000px stitched.

segments._: Section 0 - new opening plate, added ahead of garden.png. Same forest/road as garden.png (all 7 guardrail gates passed: vertical road, painted style and color match confirmed side by side against garden.png's top edge, detect_road agrees with manual measurement (centre ~1377 vs ~1377-1381, width ~156 vs ~153-182), single clean asphalt band with no competing gray structure, native 2752x1536 matching neighbor resolution, terrain genuinely continues into garden.png's opening rather than a hard cut). Painted-in car removed via tools/strip-car.py; its default PAD/feather (26px/14) left a visible seam band on this plate's more mottled road texture, so PAD was widened to 70 and the feather to 40 (both now the script's default) to keep the blend ramp outside the car's own silhouette - narrower feather ghosted the car's pale nose/bumper back in.
opening leg - dense flowering forest, car removed cleanly via strip-car.py. Trimmed shorter so the beach reveal in garden-beach.png comes up sooner.

garden opens out into a beach and turquoise water in the bottom right. garden.png's ending (a rock cluster, sparse trailside flowers) and this plate's top (palms, a different rock arrangement, a path curving in from the left) are different compositions, not the same terrain continuing - the old 200px overlap averaged the two into a soft double-exposure ghost across the seam, wide enough to read as blur. A hard cut (0) instead swapped that for a flat brightness/tone step with no transition, which read as broken too. 32px is short enough that mismatched content doesn't have room to double-expose, while still softening the step into a quick dissolve rather than a jump cut. wide:1758 added to match section 3's canvas width - this plate's own avail (~1906px) supports it, so it's not a crop change, just rendering at the same frame width as beach-cove instead of the narrower 1510 base (which garden.png, the narrowest plate in the route, forces everyone else down to by default).

the offshore islet and second boat this segment is for. Top 450px cropped off. Stops shifted -450 to match. overlap:200 with impose:true - section 2's last 200px are dropped/covered, section 3's own full (post-crop) head is what shows there, genuinely imposed on top. blend:6 (3px/side) - 0 (hard cut) and 14 (soft/flat band) were both tried; 6 softens the seam without the flat-haze look 14 had. wide:1758 (5% narrower than the 1850 that first reached the islet; avail caps at ~1855) so the frame reaches the islet, which sits ~930px right of the road centre. The extra width on garden.png/garden-beach.png's rows is transparent padding, not stretched pixels. Native 2752x1536.

Section 3 - the route continues past the cove into rolling green hills (pines, boulders, wildflowers, matching project/art/hills-l.jpg and hills-r.jpg). All 7 guardrail gates passed: vertical road in a wide canvas, painted style confirmed side by side against beach-cove-v3.png's bottom edge (jungle continues into jungle, sand into sand, the same boat visible at both edges), detect_road agrees with manual measurement (mean centre ~1393 vs ~1391-1393 on clean rows, mean width ~131 vs ~135-138), no car painted in (0 pink-on-road hits, nothing to strip), native 2752x1536 matching every other plate's resolution. The turquoise ocean/boat wake in the top-right corner does form a second low-saturation blob in the asphalt mask, but it sits entirely in the top ~15% of the frame - outside detect_road's own 15%-85% voting window - and never rivals the road's length or width; it did not affect detection. overlap:200 (the manifest default) since this is genuine continuing terrain across the seam, not a hard cut like garden-beach.png needed.

Section 4 - hills open onto a reservoir (left) and an Indian-style gravity dam with 4 gates (right), road flush against both with no buffer, ending back into plain grassy bank. Style/colour and terrain continuity confirmed side by side against beach-hills.png's bottom edge - a strong match after several regeneration rounds spent correcting hue (too golden-yellow at first) and brightness (overcorrected too dark next) against this exact reference. Source was 2048x2080 (neighbours are 2752px) - pre-upscaled with Lanczos + UnsharpMask(radius=2, percent=150, threshold=2) per Gate 7, saved over the original at 2752x2795. Gate 3/4 FAILED for this plate: detect_road tracked only 25-32% of rows even after the upscale, because the dam's concrete face, inspection walkway and stone retaining wall read as the same tone and value as the actual asphalt in this generated image - not just hard for the mask threshold, confirmed by eye at the pixel level too (sampled row 1200: no clean value jump anywhere across the road/dam boundary). The two unambiguous stretches (hillside before and after the dam, y=0-400 and y=2500-2795) were measured by hand instead: centre ~1395px, width ~170px, constant, matching a straight road. Passed as the 'road' override to plate_scale() rather than trusting detect_road's output, which locks onto the dam/wall as one wide competing band for the whole middle section - see build-ribbon.py's manual_road parameter, added for this plate.

Section 5 (final) - route closer, forest 'life goes on' theme continuing directly from dam-reservoir.png's grassy bank ending: mossy stumps with fresh saplings/shoots, a fallen mossy log with new growth, moss-softened boulders, pink/peach/gold wildflowers only (no purple/lavender - confirmed clean by eye, no HSV patch pass needed). Generated via Gemini using two reference images (dam-reservoir.png's bottom 500px for the join, garden-lead.png for style/detail density) plus an explicit hard-edge constraint added after a first generation attempt showed canopy/bushes overhanging and obscuring the road near the bottom of the frame - the corrected prompt told the generator to keep the road a clean, unbroken, unobstructed band at every row and only let forest density increase into the existing grass/floor area, not onto the road. Second attempt passed Gate 6 cleanly at every row, including the dense-forest bottom third that failed before. Pre-upscaled to 2752px wide via Lanczos + UnsharpMask(radius=2, percent=150, threshold=2) per Gate 7. Road measured ~0.10-0.12 ratio via visual gridline crops at 3 rows (consistent, clean straight edges - no foliage-noise ambiguity this time) - too wide vs the 0.062 target set by dam-reservoir/garden - fixed via the direct pixel-edit squeeze technique (isolate asphalt-core band wider than the road at every row, Lanczos-resize narrower, reassemble left+band+right), taking the plate from 2752px down to 2555px wide with no visible seam at the squeeze boundary. Gate 3 auto-detect FAILED here too (same class of failure as dam-reservoir/creek-conclusion generally - road texture grain breaks the low-saturation mask threshold) - centre/width passed as manual 'road' override instead, width tuned from an initial 166px estimate down to 160px after a first build came back at 1446px frame width (below the 1500px baseline) - recomputed the exact width needed from plate_scale()'s avail formula rather than guessing again, confirmed via rebuild: frame width 1500px, road drift 0.0px.
